class.name: NetwDisplayBook
class.brief_description: What the display plane holds for one entity, addressed by either of the entity's two names.
class.description:
An entity is named twice on the display plane: by its [RID], which is what a caller holds, and by its ROUTE, which is what the network delivers and what liveness retires. Those are two names for one thing, so they are two indexes over one row rather than two tables that can disagree. A row carries the entity's declaration and its pump runtime, and it may hold either alone. A declaration lands as soon as a caller configures the entity, which is before it goes live and therefore before it has a route or a runtime at all. [codeblock] book.set_decl(entity, decl) # configured, not yet live book.enroll(entity, route) # live: the second name arrives book.set_runtime(entity, runtime)
for runtime in book.runtimes(): # enrolment order, rows that hold one pump(runtime)
book.drop_route(route) # dead: the WHOLE row goes [/codeblock] Retiring by route drops the row and every column in it, which is what stops a declaration outliving the entity it describes. A book that had to ask a weak reference for the entity behind a dying route would leak that declaration whenever the entity was freed first, and an [RID] the engine later reuses would find it. The book also holds which entities need their channel table rebuilt. That set lives here rather than beside the rebuilder because the writes that invalidate a table address an entity by [RID] and know nothing about runtimes: a write can land before the entity is live, and the entity it names still has to be repaired once it is. [codeblock] book.write_param(entity, decl, param, value) # -> went_dirty(entity, dirt)
for entity in book.take_dirty(): # at the session's settle rebuild(entity) [/codeblock]

method.name: clear
method.description: Forgets every row under both names, which is where a session teardown ends.

method.name: clear_dirty
method.description: Withdraws [param entity]'s mark, for a listener that repaired it on the spot and has nothing left to settle. An unmarked entity is not an error.

method.name: decl_of
method.description: The declaration recorded for [param entity], or [code]null[/code] when none was.

method.name: drop
method.description: Forgets [param entity]'s row and releases the route it held, if it held one. A pending rebuild goes with it, because an entity that is gone has nothing left to repair.

method.name: drop_route
method.description: Forgets the row [param route] names, declaration included. This is retirement: a route the session has retired names an entity that is gone, so nothing it held has a reader left.

method.name: enroll
method.description: Gives [param entity]'s row its second name. Enrolling an entity that already holds a different route releases the old one, so a stale route answers nothing rather than answering a row that has moved. A [param route] of zero means the entity has no route yet, which is the state a configured but not yet live entity is in.

method.name: entity_at
method.description: The entity [param route] names, or an invalid [RID] when no row holds it.

method.name: is_dirty
method.description: Whether [param entity] is waiting for a rebuild.

method.name: mark_dirty
method.description: Reports that [param entity] needs the repair [param dirt] names, one of [enum NetwDisplayDecl.Dirt], and emits [signal went_dirty] carrying it. [constant NetwDisplayDecl.DIRT_RUNTIME] also records the entity and raises [member NetwDisplayRuntime.rebuild_queued] when a runtime already stands behind it, because rebuilding a channel table is what a listener defers. Marking an entity that is already marked does nothing and emits nothing, so a cascade of writes to one entity costs one repair. [constant NetwDisplayDecl.DIRT_ROLE] is reported and not recorded: re-resolving which source a display reads keeps the channel table it already built, so there is nothing for a drain to do. [constant NetwDisplayDecl.DIRT_NONE] and an invalid [param entity] are ignored. An entity the book has no row for is still recorded: it names an entity configured before it went live, which is the case the signal exists to let a listener answer differently.

method.name: route_of
method.description: The route [param entity] holds, or [code]0[/code] when it holds none and when the book has no row for it at all.

method.name: runtime_at
method.description: The pump runtime behind [param route], or [code]null[/code] when no row holds one.

method.name: runtime_of
method.description: The pump runtime behind [param entity], or [code]null[/code] when no row holds one. The same answer [method runtime_at] gives for that entity's route, reached without going through the route at all.

method.name: runtimes
method.description: Every runtime the book holds, in enrolment order, skipping the rows that carry only a declaration. The order is published because a pump reads it every frame, and two runs of one session showing the same sequence is what makes a display trace comparable.

method.name: set_decl
method.description: Records [param entity]'s declaration, creating its row if the entity has none yet.

method.name: set_runtime
method.description: Records [param entity]'s pump runtime, creating its row if the entity has none yet.

method.name: size
method.description: How many rows the book holds, counting a row that carries only a declaration.

method.name: take_dirty
method.description: Every entity still marked, in the order they were marked, and the set is empty afterwards. Taking the whole set rather than one entity at a time is what stops a repair stranding the rest: draining one entity would leave every other mark standing with its [member NetwDisplayRuntime.rebuild_queued] already raised, and so nothing left to raise it again.

method.name: write_param
method.description: Writes one [enum NetwDisplayDecl.Param] onto [param entity]'s declaration, reports the repair it owes through [method mark_dirty], and answers which of [enum NetwDisplayDecl.Dirt] that was. [param decl] is the declaration to publish if the book holds none for [param entity] yet, which is how a caller hands over the record it authored before the entity was live. A book that already holds one keeps it and ignores [param decl], so a second caller cannot replace a record other settings have already landed on.

signal.name: went_dirty
signal.description: Emitted once per repair [method mark_dirty] newly reports, carrying the entity and which of [enum NetwDisplayDecl.Dirt] is owed. It carries the entity because what a repair costs depends on which one it is: an entity with a runtime can wait for a settle, and one without has nothing on screen to wait with.
